Bhāguri
grammarian an. Lexicographer. son of Bhagura, disciple of Bṛhat Garga.
Contributed to several branches of Skt. lit.; lived prior to Pāṇini a. known from the quote in Nyāsa (vaSTi bhAgurirallopA).
Ref. by Jinendrabuddhi (Nyāsa on Kāśikā 6-2-37) an. Jagadīśa Tarkālaṅkāra (Patañjali refers to Bhagurī I. 7-3-45, possibly a scholarly sister of Bhāguri).
A number of references to his works on Lexicography, Poetics, Brāhmaṇa exegesis, an. Politics are found.
See JBORS. XI. (1925) 69; also Dict. of. Skt. Gr. p. 291b. [Page329-a.
Ved.
wrote expositions (?) on Sāmaveda, Yajurveda an. also a Brāhmaṇa text, Bhāguri Brāhmaṇa. See Vaidik Vāṅmay Kā itihās. I. ii. p. 181.
Alaṅkāra
q. by Someśvara in his Sāhityakalpadruma on Yathāsaṅkhyālaṅkāra, MT. 2126 an. by Abhinavagupta in Dhvanyāloka, Uddyota III, p. 385.
Lexicography:
His quotes are found in Amarakośa (Ṭīkāsarvasva an. in Bhāṣāvṛtti. This work was prob. called Trikāṇḍa). He is quoted several times in Bṛhaddevatā; also by Lakṣmīdhara on Manusmṛtibhāṣya (8/ 198); an. by Somadeva in Yaśastilakacampū a. a writer on Rājanītiśāstra.
From quotations referring to him in grammatical treatises viz., Śabdaśaktiprakāśikā, it seems he was the a. of a Dhātupāṭha (guNo vadhezca nindAyAM etc.).
For add.. details about a. see Y. Mimamsak. Sam. Vyā. Kā itihas. I. p.. 112-17; II. p.. 27-28. 147-48.
Following works are found in his name:
-Mayūracitra. jy. Bṛhatsūci, Nepal I. p.. 148-49.
-Sūtakanirṇaya from his Smṛtisārasamuccaya. dh. NPS. II. p. 544.
-Smṛtisārasamuccaya. IO. II. 5549. RASB. III. 1914-15. Śṛṅgerī Mutt 124. Viz. Skt. Col.. Wai D. I. 3564 (Bhāruci). [Page329-b]
